title: The Sando Project brings Japanese milk-bread sandos to Chennai and Puducherry
excerpt: Ciclo Café's limited-time Sando Project menu piles Indo-Chinese chilli chicken, bibimbap paneer and beef fillet with mustard into thick, in-house Japanese milk bread across Chennai and Puducherry.
body:
• Ciclo Café in Chennai and Puducherry is running a limited-time menu called The Sando Project, built around Japanese milk-bread sandos with messy, indulgent fillings.
  • The lineup spans a bibimbap paneer sando, a chilli chicken sando, a beef fillet sando with mustard and smoky BBQ sauce, and a chicken caesar — all breads and fillings made in-house.
  • The menu pairs the sandos with thick, dessert-like shakes, including a Milo dino and a Lotus biscoff shake.
  • The Sando Project is the latest sign of Chennai's fast-evolving café scene embracing Japanese-format sandwiches done in local flavours.

Japanese milk bread has found a new home on India's southeast coast. Ciclo Café is running a limited-time menu called The Sando Project across its Chennai and Puducherry outlets — a full lineup of sandos built on thick, pillowy Japanese milk bread, loaded with crispy, juicy fillings and finished with deliberately messy sauces.

The format is a spin on the Japanese sando, where the bread is as important as what goes inside it. Here, every loaf and filling is made in-house, and the milk bread is soft enough to compress slightly when pressed — only to spring back. The result, as a tasting by Indulge Express found, is a sandwich where the bread does real work: soaking up sauce at the edges without collapsing.

What is on the menu

The lineup mixes vegetarian and non-vegetarian options with a distinctly cross-cultural pantry. The bibimbap paneer sando was judged one of the best vegetarian sandos on the menu — stir-fried paneer and vegetables lifted by a Korean spicy sauce that gives genuine heat. The chilli chicken sando goes Indo-Chinese: tender chicken, crunchy peppers and onions, and an Indo-Chinese chilli sauce that, per the tasting, makes no mistakes.

The beef fillet with mustard sando is the one to order if there is only room for one: beef tenderloin strips in a smoky BBQ sauce with caramelised onions and melted cheddar, with the mustard sitting behind the richness and keeping it honest.

"We ate it and said very little to each other, which is its own kind of praise."

— Indulge Express, on the beef fillet sando

The chicken caesar is the composed, quiet option of the set — grilled chicken, crisp romaine and a properly made Caesar dressing inside toasted milk bread. No gimmicks, just a cheesy, comforting sando.

Palate cleansers between bites

Between the sandos, the menu's beverage pairing leans fully into indulgence. The Milo dino shake, singled out as the favourite, is thick and deeply chocolatey — almost a meal in itself. The Lotus biscoff shake is more restrained: smooth and caramel-warm, a calmer counterpoint to the savoury heaviness.

Sandos are having a Chennai moment

The Sando Project lands at a time when Chennai's café scene is leaning hard into sandwich experimentation. Owner-led diners in the city have been building dramatic milk-bread sandwiches with clean halves cut open to show the fillings — a format that photographs as well as it eats. The Sando Project fits that arc: Japanese format, local flavours, theatrical presentation.

For visitors, the practical note is that this is a limited-time menu rather than a permanent fixture. If you are planning a Chennai or Puducherry stop — a home visit, a wedding trip, a holiday on the coast — check Ciclo Café's outlets before you go, and treat the menu like what it is: a seasonal detour worth one deliberate meal.
